speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) what is the intended duration of the Free Morning Off-Peak Rail Rides scheme on the North East Line (NEL); (b) whether the Government is committed to making the scheme permanent in order to drive a sustained shift in travel patterns; and (c) if so, whether that commitment is contingent on plans to further increase NEL peak-hour capacity, if any.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: By shifting a small proportion of peak hour commuters who are able and willing to travel off-peak, we improve the commuting experience for those who still have to travel when it is most crowded.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Redistributing the peak load also enables the overall capacity of the train line to be more efficiently used.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Furthermore, a smaller peak load will reduce the impact of a train delay or disruption, if it happens.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If we are able to achieve a similar and sustained result, we will not need to have additional resources to support higher commuter traffic before 7.30 am.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: First, I understand from the CNA article that when speaking to the reporters back then, the Minister shared that the peak hour passenger load on the NEL is not close to the Land Transport Authority's (LTA's) operating performance standards.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I was wondering if the Minister can elaborate on this, because in relation to an earlier Parliamentary Question I filed in September, I had asked about the maximum passengers per hour per direction and capacity utilisation during peak hours.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, if the Acting Minister can give us a sense of these numbers to understand where it is today and where is the ideal level that LTA is looking at.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is in relation to the NEL today.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Are there any technical limitations to increasing the frequency further in terms of reducing the time between trains or even, let us say, increasing it from the current six cars to seven or eight, depending on the possibilities?

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: In terms of the technical limitations of improving the capacity of the train lines, the free off-peak travel programme is one of a suite of measures that we have to try to manage the overall capacity of the train in terms of optimising it, but also to reduce the peak level crowding.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: Beyond that, we have been adding new trains to the NEL over the years.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: We have improved the signalling systems so that the headways between the trains have come down significantly.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: Outside of the train system, we have also added City Direct buses to bring people from their residence in the North East to the city centre.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: As for whether or not we can add more train carriages, that is often suggested.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, we have not taken that step yet.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: What we have done is, for future lines, going forward, to see if we can budget for stations that are longer, in advance, and then, perhaps, in future, to only have smaller capacity trains and to extend the capacity of those trains when we need to.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The other question is, what is the expected revenue leakage and is this sustainable in the long run?

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: In terms of more resources, as I had mentioned in my reply, if the outcome of the programme is around what we expect, which is hopefully about 7% of the peak hour load shifted to off-peak, then there is enough capacity during the off-peak and we will not need additional resources before 7.30 am.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: The programme as of now, as a pilot, is fully funded by the Government.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, there are no additional resources that are needed.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: The revenue loss to the system is entirely covered by the Government.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: But what actually will be the Government expenditure on the scheme really depends on the take-up of the scheme.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I have got two supplemental questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first is, whether the programme is expected to result in net positive movement in congestion and what are the considerations?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Taking into account that there is a quite a number of Build-To-Order (BTO) and condominium projects coming up, will that be taken into account when deciding whether to continue this programme?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The second supplemental question is, earlier, my colleague Mr Chua said about the 7% shift from when we did a similar project in 2013.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I am just wondering what happens if we hit or we do not hit that 7%?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What is the decision going to be either way?

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: On the whole, in the longer term, what agencies do is they do plan the transport infrastructure and the capacity of the transport infrastructure in tandem with housing developments.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: And housing is about five years for a new BTO estate.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, they try to make sure that is synchronised.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: But in the short term, on a year-to-year basis, we also make continuous adjustments, whether it is adding new buses or in this case, proposing this free off-peak travel scheme.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: And I think overall the objective is to optimise the capacity of the train network, in particular, of specific trains during peak hours and to make for a better travel experience for our commuters.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, we should see the free travel scheme as part of that series of continuous adjustments.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, whether the Ministry can shed light on the thought processes and data types selecting only the NEL and Sengkang-Punggol LRT for the free off-peak pilot – as you know, Bishan is a very crowded station with two lines as well – rather than other high congestion interchange stations.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second question is to ask the Acting Minister for Transport whether the Ministry has conducted an accessibility impact assessment to determine whether the free off-peak scheme will disproportionately benefit able-bodied commuters who can flexibly adjust their travel timing, while vulnerable commuters such as persons with disabilities, elderly commuters and parents with young children who may have inflexible schedules due to work, school, medical appointments, or childcare constraints, will gain minimal benefit?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And whether the Ministry will consider alternative subsidy mechanisms targeting vulnerable commuters with fixed schedules?

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: The first is that this is the most well used part of our MRT network at present and we think we want to see whether we can optimise the off-peak crowding on that line.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: The second reason is that for parts of the NEL that are above Kovan station at the moment, they do not have an alternative route to the MRT network, until the Cross Island Line is built in five years time.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: And so, should there be a disruption and when there is a disruption, actually, the impact is quite significant to manage.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: Therefore, it is in our interest to try to reduce the peak hour crowding as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: Bishan, in relative terms, is slightly less crowded, more well-connected.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, for the moment, we have decided to keep the pilot to the NEL.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: On the second question on accessibility, I fully understand the Member's concerns.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: Our objective with the scheme is to move a small proportion of those who are able and willing to move from peak hour travel to off-peak.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: And we are giving them a little incentive to do so.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: This will not only benefit these commuters, but it will also benefit the commuters who have no choice but to travel during the more crowded periods.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: It will benefit them through having less crowded trains, hopefully shorter waiting times for the trains and generally a better commuter experience for them.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: So, it is a win-win situation for all.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: And more broadly, beyond that, accessibility considerations are very much top of our priority when it comes to public transport.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: We will be very sure to focus on that.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Nevertheless, when you look at the loading in the North East area, I think this good initiative is but a interim measure – whether it is the buses where in the previous question, Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling told me that the buses loading versus MRT capacity is a great difference.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: So, my simple supplementary question is, with this good initiative, would the Seletar Line be accelerated?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: Because, ultimately, with all the housing density being built up in the North East region, whether in Punggol or in Jalan Kayu, including Sengkang, I think fundamentally, a new MRT line would be needed.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
text: And if you can consider accelerating the Seletar Line, it would be very much appreciated by many residents in the North East region.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: As I explained earlier, the planning of an MRT line is in tandem with housing developments and travel demand.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: These are longer-term plans which the agencies work together very closely and we try to make sure that there is enough travel capacity to accommodate the demand for the long term.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: In the short term, we do make adjustments in terms of continual improvements, whether it is adding new buses to the transport corridor, whether it is introducing the free off-peak travel scheme.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: These are short-term adjustments that we try to make, to make sure that the commuters' travel demands can be adequately catered for.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: I hope to have an update on this sometime across the turn of the year and most probably during the Committee of Supply period.

speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
text: But we will take a look at it and let LTA do its work to study the line.
